title: The Living Loop
subtitle: Follow the garden into the rooms that keep it growing.
intro: Mel’s marigolds are one small part of a much larger exchange. Step behind the garden: meet the growers, follow the water, and discover what can become food again.
proposal: A proposed farm cluster serving the neighborhood of Floor 318. The rooms, scale and connections are an architectural study, not a confirmed floor plan or a claim of food self-sufficiency.

places.label: The growing room
places.eyebrow: Start with something you can taste
places.description: A tomato picked for tonight’s table. Leafy greens in water-fed channels. Soil beds for the community garden. These can be neighbors without receiving the same inputs.
places.exchange: Hydroponics receives measured, conditioned fish-water nutrients plus any missing minerals. Mature compost belongs in suitable soil or substrate beds; it does not circulate through the fish tanks.
places.care: Proposed routine: growers inspect roots, taste harvests and check crop-specific light and nutrition. Plant-water recirculation has its own reservoir and controls.
places.ai: The illustrated drone scouts leaves and fruit for visible changes. Greenhouse monitoring drones already exist; this particular body and deployment are a proposal. An AI grower could combine those observations with crop plans and irrigation data. People still assess flavor and texture.
places.quality: Track marketable harvest, flavor, texture, nutrient composition and shelf life alongside water and energy per edible kilogram.

places.label: The fish room
places.description: Fish need a dependable life-support system of their own. Mechanical filtration removes solids; a biological filter processes dissolved nitrogen waste; aeration and circulation keep the system working.
places.exchange: Feed brings nutrients into the farm. Some leave as harvested fish; some become recoverable waste. A portion of treated water can supply plants, without plant water returning to the fish.
places.care: Proposed safeguards: independently isolatable tanks, backup oxygen and power, and staff who check behavior as well as instruments. Stocking depends on biomass, species and treatment capacity.
places.ai: One floating monitor in each tank is our proposed way to carry cameras and water sensors. Camera-based appetite and biomass estimates can assist feeding, but the skimmer bodies are concept designs, not ReelData products. Validate sensing for the actual species, lighting and water clarity.
places.quality: Measure survival, welfare, feed conversion and edible product quality, not simply the number of fish in a tank.

places.label: The water workshop
places.description: This is where an exchange becomes deliberate. Solids separation, biofiltration and water-quality checks support the fish circuit. A controlled transfer supplies the independently managed plant circuit.
places.exchange: Captured sludge takes a separate recovery route. Mineralization can release nutrients, but the resulting liquid needs analysis and conditioning before a crop-specific dose is considered.
places.care: Proposed routine: check oxygen, temperature, pH, ammonia species, nitrite and individual nutrients. Electrical conductivity alone cannot show whether the nutrient mix is balanced.
places.ai: An AI operator could flag sensor disagreement and recommend a hold on transfers. Independent alarms and local controls must still work if its model or network is unavailable.
places.quality: Release batches against defined nutrient and contaminant specifications. Record where each batch came from and where it went.

places.label: The mushroom room
places.description: Oyster mushrooms can turn suitable fibrous materials into another harvest. Prepared straw or compatible woody substrate is a more grounded starting point than a promise that every waste stream can grow mushrooms.
places.exchange: Selected crop residues need a tested substrate recipe and appropriate preparation. Spent substrate can join managed composting after assessment; it is not automatically ready to spread.
places.care: Proposed layout: a separate room with its own humidity, ventilation and clean handling. Species and substrate determine the cultivation method.
places.ai: Our proposed ceiling arms pick mushrooms and load the container built into a small quad’s back. Current commercial harvesting robots are a useful comparison; this ceiling-mounted arrangement and its suitability for oyster mushrooms still need development.
places.quality: Observe contamination, cap development, bruising, marketable harvest and storage quality.

places.label: The insect nursery
places.description: Black soldier fly larvae can convert selected organic side streams into feed ingredients. This is animal husbandry: substrate, climate, hygiene and harvest handling all matter.
places.exchange: Route suitable vegetable and food-production trimmings here. Processed larvae may replace part of a formulated fish diet after species-specific nutrition and product-quality trials.
places.care: Proposed boundary: traceable, approved feedstocks only. Keep incompatible or contaminated waste out. Frass and uneaten substrate need a defined treatment route before use on crops.
places.ai: Automation could track tray conditions and batches. Any model must be tested against actual larvae growth, substrate variation and harvested ingredient composition.
places.quality: Check ingredient safety, protein and fat composition, digestibility and the quality of fish fed that diet.

places.label: The return to soil
places.eyebrow: Finishing is part of the process
places.description: Managed aerobic composting turns appropriate residues into a stable soil amendment. It needs oxygen, moisture management and time to mature. A closed vessel can contain odors without making the process anaerobic.
places.exchange: Selected plant residues, spent mushroom substrate and suitable insect residues converge here. Finished, assessed compost returns to soil beds. It is not a pipe into hydroponics or fish water.
places.care: Proposed layout: an enclosed service bay with separate ventilation, leachate collection and access for maintenance. Larger-volume processing may belong at a shared city utility.
places.ai: A worker loads assessed compost into a dirt-hauling quad’s large back bucket. This proposed body makes the load and its destination visible. Sensors and controls could track the composting process; a completion prediction does not replace maturity and product-quality checks.
places.quality: Check stability, maturity, salts, contaminants and suitability for the intended crop or landscape.

routes.label: Follow the water
routes.intro: Two recirculating circuits. One controlled exchange.
routes.boundary: Fish life support and plant irrigation operate separately. Nutrient transfer can stop without making either circuit depend on the other’s return water.

steps.label: Fish water → water care
steps.detail: Separate solids, process dissolved nitrogen waste and maintain oxygen.

steps.label: Water care → fish
steps.detail: The fish circuit recirculates locally; it does not depend on plant drainage.

steps.label: Tested transfer → hydroponics
steps.detail: A controlled amount moves one way. Adjust the plant reservoir for the crop’s needs.

steps.label: Plant reservoir → plants → reservoir
steps.detail: Plants have their own recirculation, replenishment and nutrient management.

routes.label: Follow the harvest
routes.intro: Keep food in the kitchen. Give suitable leftovers another use.
routes.boundary: This is a branching network, not a conveyor belt through every organism. Fish are the animal module shown here. Other livestock would need their own space, feed, welfare and waste assessment.

steps.label: Edible harvest → neighbors
steps.detail: Plants, fish and mushrooms leave the farm as food. Those nutrients do not magically return.

steps.label: Suitable fibrous residues → mushrooms
steps.detail: Use a compatible, prepared substrate recipe; additional straw or wood may be needed.

steps.label: Suitable trimmings → insect nursery
steps.detail: Sort and assess feedstock before rearing. Not every organic residue is acceptable.

steps.label: Processed larvae → formulated fish feed
steps.detail: An ingredient in a balanced diet, with safety and quality checks—not a complete feed by default.

routes.label: Follow the return
routes.intro: The route back has several gates.
routes.boundary: Recovery reduces losses; it does not eliminate them. The farm still needs energy, replacement water, feed or substrates and nutrient supplementation, with outlets for rejected material.

steps.label: Selected plant residues → composting
steps.detail: Separate material suitable for compost from contaminated or otherwise unsuitable residues.

steps.label: Spent mushroom substrate → composting
steps.detail: Assess the spent substrate and blend it with other appropriate materials.

steps.label: Insect residues → treatment and composting
steps.detail: Frass needs processing and suitability checks before crop use.

steps.label: Mature compost → soil beds
steps.detail: Return an assessed amendment to the soil garden, not the hydroponic reservoir.

steps.label: Captured fish solids → separate nutrient recovery
steps.detail: A potential mineralization process, followed by analysis and conditioning. Neither untreated sludge nor digestate goes straight to crops.

sources.title: Adel et al. · Drones-of-the-Future in Agriculture 5.0
sources.scope: Author-supplied reference. Publisher abstract and indexed text reviewed. Examines Drone-as-a-Service, including crop monitoring and integration; it is not a trial of this indoor farm or evidence that images alone establish eating quality. DOI: 10.1016/j.agsy.2025.104543.

sources.title: Monsees, Kloas & Wuertz · Decoupled systems on trial
sources.scope: Five-month pilot comparing coupled and decoupled aquaponics with a RAS control. Supports independent water management; its crop results are not an Arcology yield forecast.

sources.title: Tetreault et al. · Parallel unit process aquaponics
sources.scope: Hypothesis-and-theory article on component-specific hydraulic retention times. Also explains costs and space tradeoffs of separate systems. Not proof that decoupling is always best.

sources.title: Gerdes genannt Janßen et al. · Nutrient recovery from aquaculture sludge
sources.scope: Treatment experiments on commercial tilapia sludge show different nutrient profiles and conditioning needs. Downstream growth tests used Arthrospira; they do not establish universal vegetable safety or yield.

sources.title: Cornell Small Farms · Methods of commercial mushroom cultivation
sources.scope: Species, substrate preparation and cultivation methods. Supports a prepared oyster-mushroom substrate route, not a universal waste-to-mushrooms claim.

sources.title: Eawag · Black soldier fly biowaste processing
sources.scope: Operational guidance and research on insect rearing, conversion and post-processing. Biological convertibility does not establish food/feed permission or safety for every substrate.

sources.title: Aquaculture Reports · Insect meal and salmon fillet quality
sources.scope: A full-production-cycle sea-cage salmon study examining fillet and sensory quality. Relevant questions for diet trials; not transferable performance data for indoor tilapia. Bibliographic abstract reviewed.

sources.title: US EPA · Composting
sources.scope: Defines aerobic composting and stable compost, and distinguishes them from anaerobic digestion and unfinished material.

sources.title: Wageningen · Autonomous Greenhouse Challenge
sources.scope: Real greenhouse trials of AI crop control, with crop-specific datasets and papers linked. Demonstrates practical experimentation, not a single guaranteed savings or accuracy rate.

sources.title: Source.ag · AI irrigation and cultivation
sources.scope: A greenhouse comparison. The case describes pilot experience and grower oversight; it does not validate our mixed crops or promise better flavor or nutrition.

company.application: Models help growers plan cultivation, forecast harvests and control irrigation.
company.deployment: Source describes Rainbow Growers Middenmeer using its irrigation control with peppers, including the growers’ experience of the pilot.

sources.title: Corvus Drones · Greenhouse scouting robots
sources.scope: Supports indoor crop scouting. Images cannot establish flavor or nutritional composition.

company.application: Autonomous drones observe greenhouse crops and count germination.
company.deployment: Corvus names Plantenkwekerij Gitzels as a user monitoring potato seedlings.

sources.title: ReelData · AI feeding for land-based fish farms
sources.scope: Relevant to land-based tanks. This is camera-and-feeder automation, not the illustrated floating robot; performance must be checked for our species and water conditions.

company.application: ReelAppetite detects uneaten pellets in tank outflows and adjusts connected feeders.
company.deployment: An October 2024 announcement describes over a year of use at Samherji’s Staður charr site, followed by an agreement covering three sites. The agreement alone does not confirm every installation was completed.

sources.title: Aquaai · Mobile underwater sensing
sources.scope: Underwater fishlike robots, not surface skimmers. No named farm installation verified here.

company.application: Fishlike robots carry cameras and sensors for water monitoring.
company.deployment: Aquaai offers service or demonstration access and describes autonomous navigation and computer vision.

sources.title: Gradiant / Turing · AI water-process optimization
sources.scope: Evidence for AI assisting water-plant operations. Desalination is a different process from aquaponic biofiltration or safe nutrient transfer; no savings percentage is carried into our design.

company.application: SmartOps uses operating data to model water-treatment performance and recommend adjustments.
company.deployment: Gradiant’s ENGIE case describes machine-learning recommendations at a Middle Eastern seawater desalination plant, online in 2021. Operators entered the recommended settings.

sources.title: Ostara · Recovering nutrients as fertilizer
sources.scope: A supporting recovery process, not an AI or robotics example. Municipal wastewater differs from fish solids; this does not establish direct reuse in hydroponics or recovery of every nutrient.

company.application: Pearl reactors recover phosphorus in struvite fertilizer granules from suitable wastewater streams.
company.deployment: Ostara and Chicago’s MWRD opened a nutrient-recovery facility at the Stickney plant in May 2016.

sources.title: 4AG Robotics · Mushroom picking, trimming and packing
sources.scope: The documented crop is Agaricus. Our oyster mushrooms, ceiling mounts and receiving quad are adaptations requiring development.

company.application: Robots pick, trim and pack mushrooms in existing growing racks.
company.deployment: In July 2025, 4AG reported live systems in Canada, Ireland and Australia. Planned deployments elsewhere are not counted as completed.

sources.title: Protix · Industrial insect rearing
sources.scope: Protix explicitly reports using AI and robotics, but the reviewed pages give limited detail on their individual tasks or measured contribution. Suitable feedstocks and fish-diet formulation remain separate questions.

company.application: Black soldier fly production converts selected industrial organic side streams into feed and farming ingredients.
company.deployment: Protix describes commercial production and a Dutch blueprint plant opened in 2019. Its operations page identifies AI and robotics among the technologies it uses.

sources.title: Engineered Compost Systems · Controlled composting
sources.scope: Conventional process automation, not a verified AI system. It supports managed composting and batch records, not our bucket-carrying quad or a promise of instant mature compost.

company.application: Sensors and controls regulate aeration, surface irrigation and process records during composting.
company.deployment: ECS describes its CompTroller installation at Napa Recycling and Waste Services, processing yard and food waste. The case includes finished compost supplied to agriculture and community gardens.

evidence.title: Napa composting installation and return to growers

sources.title: Sonnenerde · Autonomous compost-turning research
sources.scope: A field-tested prototype, not a verified commercial robot fleet. Outdoor satellite navigation and windrows differ from an indoor compost bay; autonomous control does not by itself establish machine learning.

company.status: Prototype tested in an industrial setting
company.application: A compost producer helped develop autonomous electric compost turning with Pusch & Schinnerl and university partners.
company.deployment: The ANDREA project names Sonnenerde as coordinator. The researchers’ 2024 report describes an autonomous turner tested in three industrial-site scenarios.
